summary: A music failure now raises an alert and leaves evidence behind, instead of sitting green until someone in the room notices.
details: There was no music metric of any kind before this — not uncollected, never declared — so no alert rule could be written. A live wedge sat with every light green: the containers reported healthy, Prometheus had nothing to say, and the only thing that ever noticed was a person listening.

Two series carry the divergence rather than a derived verdict: `nora_music_expected_playing` is what nora believes, `nora_music_controller_playing` is what the audio controller reports. The judgement stays in the alert expression instead of being baked into one 'healthy' flag in code.
`nora_music_liveness_total{verdict}` counts every poll by decided verdict, and `nora_music_stream_failed_total{reason}` counts streams that failed after nora believed they were playing.

Three alerts: MusicWedged (belief and controller disagree for 2 minutes, critical), MusicControllerUnreadable (nora could not read the controller for 10 minutes, warning), MusicStreamFailing (3 failures in 15 minutes, warning). They route over the Alertmanager path that already delivers to Discord.

When nora cannot read the controller the playing gauge is left ABSENT, never set to 0. A gauge that could not be measured must not assert a value: 0 would read as 'definitely not playing' and fire the wedge alert off a network blip. The alert's `unless` depends on absence, and a test pins it.

The audio controller now mirrors its log into its state volume. `docker logs` keeps nothing across `up -d --force-recreate`, which is the command every deploy runs, so the loop had been: music breaks, restart to restore service, the evidence is destroyed by the act of restoring it, the mechanism is guessed at. ffmpeg's stderr tail — the line that names the cause — crosses to nora in no event at all and died with the container every time.
The four unrotated services also gained the log rotation stanza two other services already had, so an unbounded file cannot grow on disk.
limitations: The mirrored log keeps one generation back at 16MB, so a failure older than roughly two files is still lost.
The alerts describe divergence and unreadability; they do not name a cause. The sidecar log, now preserved, is still what does that.
